message.content:
When it comes to jazz vocalists, several names consistently stand out as some of the best and most influential in the genre:

| Singer | Notable Contributions | Why They’re Considered Among the Best |
|--------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered a deeply emotive, conversational style; iconic recordings like “Strange Fruit” and “God Bless the Child.” | Her phrasing and emotional depth set a new standard for jazz singing. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she mastered scat singing and had impeccable diction. | Her technical mastery and versatility across many styles earned her universal acclaim. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Possessed a rich, operatic voice with incredible range and control. | Her blend of jazz and classical techniques made her one of the most versatile vocalists. |
| **Nina Simone** | Combined jazz, blues, and classical influences; powerful political activism through music. | Her unique voice and lyrical storytelling made her a cultural icon. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Modern jazz vocalist who blends folk, blues, and world music. | Her innovative approach and deep, resonant tone keep her at the forefront of contemporary jazz. |

These artists have left indelible marks on jazz history, each bringing a distinct voice and style that continues to inspire musicians and listeners alike.
